There seems to be a sudden spate of mathlib CI runs failing at the post-CI step, e.g.

https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/actions/runs/25012167640
https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/actions/runs/25009685577
https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/actions/runs/25009378150
https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/actions/runs/25008471422
They were probably caused by this GitHub incident: #rss > GitHub Status - Incident History @ 💬 . Looks like they've declared it "resolved" :fingers_crossed:
Doesn't seem to be resolved, sadly; I just re-ran CI on my failing PR and it failed at exactly the same point as before.
A bors batch failed on the "Run 8BitJonny/gh-get-current-pr@4056877062a1f3b624d5d4c2bedefa9cf51435c9" step (but I can't see any error messages).

From this run:

Run set +e
{verify Mathlib cache}
{verify Archive cache}
{verify Counterexamples cache}
Error: Cache verification failed and this PR's Cache/ matches master's, so the key spaces agree: the uploaded cache is incomplete.
Error: Process completed with exit code 1.

The error message seems like AI slop. Can someone fix this?

IMO try pushing an empty commit to rerun CI
I'm pretty sure you can ignore everything before the colon in the error message, this is just the usual "not everything was found in the cache". Specifically it seems you're missing 1 file, probably the one you changed last.
But can we fix the error message? It's worded really weirdly.
Claude detected :siren:

The FRO has an error message style guide which we should really be following here. I can't find the document itself, but the main points were to first name the error (here: "uploaded cache is incomplete"), then you can add notes for explaining the cause (so here you could detect changes to the Cache folder, and add "Note: Cache folder changed between this commit and master branch."), and hints for common fixes ("Hint: this can be a transient network error, try rerunning the failing workflow.")
I'm including tweaks to improve the language in these messages in #44940, which also addresses some flakiness in uploads that is making this issue more prominent.
